questions.q: Why does x_acme_eq_checkout extend task in this lab's design, while x_acme_eq_equipment stands alone?
options: Checkout needs a real lifecycle (Requested, Approved, Checked Out, Returned) and an assignment group; equipment is static inventory data with no workflow
Checkout is a smaller table than equipment, and smaller tables always extend task
Equipment extends task because it needs an assignment group for the IT pool
Both tables extend task, since every custom table should extend it by default
questions.explain: The deciding question from Lesson 24 is whether the entity needs routing, approval, or a state machine — true for checkout, false for equipment.

questions.q: What does the equipment_item reference field on x_acme_eq_checkout actually store and display?
options: It stores and displays identical free text describing the equipment
It stores a sys_id pointing at the equipment record while displaying a readable value, such as the item's name
It stores the equipment's asset tag as plain text with no link to the equipment table
It stores a list of every piece of equipment in inventory
questions.explain: A Reference-type field stores a sys_id underneath a readable display value, the same mechanism applied in Lesson 25's build.

questions.q: Why does requested_for exist as a separate field from whoever is submitting the checkout request?
options: Because the person submitting a checkout isn't always the same person the equipment is actually for
Because ServiceNow requires every task-extending table to have at least two reference fields
Because requested_for is actually a required field on the base task table
Because it replaces the need for an equipment_item field
questions.explain: requested_for, a reference to sys_user, exists because an admin or coordinator might submit a checkout on someone else's behalf.

questions.q: Why does the "Checkouts" module get Order 100 while "Equipment Catalog" gets Order 200?
options: Order has no effect on where a module appears in the navigator
Lower Order values must always point at task-extending tables
Checkouts is the module the equipment-pool coordinator will use constantly, so a lower Order places it above the less-frequently-used catalog module
Order 100 is required for every first module created in a scoped app
questions.explain: Order is a plain number controlling position among sibling modules; the most-used module gets the lower value so it appears first.

questions.q: What has to be true of both the "Checkouts" and "Equipment Catalog" modules for them to appear nested under the same Equipment Checkout section of the navigator?
options: Both must have their Application menu field pointing at the same sys_app_application record
Both must extend the same base table
Both must have identical Link type values
Both must share the same Order value
questions.explain: A module's Application menu field is what nests it under a specific top-level entry — both modules point at the same Equipment Checkout menu record.
